title: arXiv Trending Physics — Friday, 6 November 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred ordering is a notable-recent-work ranking, not measured popularity. Citation evidence is limited for papers only days old.

sections.title: The cold substellar frontier in JWST Extragalactic surveys: a robust parallax measurement yields the most distant known ultra-cold Y dwarf
sections.abstract: Multi-epoch JWST imaging yields a trigonometric parallax and distance for the very cold JADES-GS-BD-5 Y-dwarf candidate, while its spectrum and luminosity make it a benchmark for cold-atmosphere models.
sections.claimed_result: The authors measure parallax 15.7^{+1.4}_{-1.3} mas and distance 64^{+6}_{-5} pc from roughly two years of JWST/NIRCam data, and infer a very low luminosity consistent with a planetary-mass object under evolutionary models.
sections.evidence_type: observational; multi-epoch JWST/NIRCam astrometry and JADES/GOODS-South spectroscopy and photometry
sections.unique_caveat: The paper notes that low resolving power and the lack of standards later than Y1 make the spectral subtype poorly defined; the planetary-mass interpretation depends on evolutionary models.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Quantified JWST parallax result, three astro-ph cross-lists, submission to MNRAS, and independent write-ups; coverage is not independent measurement.

sections.title: Observing mixed-state Uhlmann winding numbers in integrated photonic quantum walks
sections.abstract: An integrated photonic quantum-walk chip is used to observe integer winding numbers in reconstructed thermal mixed states, with several discrete changes as temperature increases.
sections.claimed_result: The authors reconstruct closed Uhlmann-overlap trajectories and observe integer windings that change discretely with temperature, distinguishing regimes that the two-valued Uhlmann phase alone cannot separate.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; integrated photonic chip programmed for quantum walks and measurements of reconstructed thermal states
sections.unique_caveat: The demonstration covers selected chiral Hamiltonians and spectrum-preserving extensions on a finite photonic platform; it does not establish the invariant's robustness for arbitrary mixed states or devices.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct hardware demonstration of a mixed-state topological quantity, plus external discussion that is not independent replication.

sections.title: First broadband search for fixed-polarization dark photon dark matter with GigaBREAD
sections.abstract: A polarization-matched reanalysis of GigaBREAD data searches for fixed-polarization dark photons from 44–52 μeV and reports no signal, setting kinetic-mixing limits around 10⁻¹².
sections.claimed_result: The authors find no fixed-polarization dark-photon signal and set limits near χ ~ 10⁻¹², about 20% stronger than a naive rescaling of the prior GigaBREAD limit.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; room-temperature broadband dish-antenna data from GigaBREAD analyzed with a time-dependent polarization-matched likelihood
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on the fixed-polarization signal model; the paper applies a frequency-dependent 23% power systematic when deriving limits.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: First search tailored to the fixed-polarization scenario, four physics cross-list categories, and a quantitative improvement over the experiment's naive rescaled limit; it is a reanalysis, not an independent experimental confirmation.

sections.title: Experimental Evidence for Type-I Superconductivity in OsB₂
sections.abstract: The author reports three experimental signatures that reclassify osmium diboride, previously treated as a low-κ Type-II superconductor, as a rare nonelemental Type-I superconductor.
sections.claimed_result: The author interprets the differential paramagnetic effect, field-induced first-order specific-heat transition, and supercooling-like hysteresis as evidence that OsB₂ is Type I rather than Type II.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; AC susceptibility, specific-heat, and field-ramped magnetic measurements
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract does not provide numerical uncertainty or sample-to-sample reproducibility details, and the reclassification remains an author-reported preprint result pending independent replication.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three distinct reported signatures and cross-listing across superconductivity and materials science; no journal reference is listed on arXiv.

sections.title: Mitigating scanning-induced systematics in Hipparcos and implications for Gaia astrometry
sections.abstract: A scan-angle-controlled extension of a periodogram suppresses scanning-law periodicities in Hipparcos and Gaia DR4 prerelease epoch astrometry while retaining known orbital signals.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report suppression of recurrent scan-related periods, including a roughly 54-day feature in multiple Gaia DR4 prerelease sources, while independently known orbital signals remain detectable.
sections.evidence_type: observational; Hipparcos measurements and Gaia DR4 prerelease epoch astrometry analyzed with a non-parametric scan-angle-controlled periodogram
sections.unique_caveat: The Gaia demonstration uses prerelease epoch data and establishes a diagnostic and mitigation method, not a complete calibration of all future DR4 companion searches.
sections.journal_reference: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for A&A, three astro-ph categories, and tests on Hipparcos and Gaia prerelease data.

sections.title: High precision timing of seven binary millisecond pulsars with the European Pulsar Timing Array
sections.abstract: European Pulsar Timing Array observations of seven binary millisecond pulsars yield improved astrometric and orbital solutions, including annual-orbital parallax signatures and gravitational-wave strain upper limits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors obtain phase-coherent timing solutions for seven binaries, measure astrometric/orbital parameters and Shapiro-delay mass constraints, and place strain upper limits in sub-nanohertz and microhertz bands.
sections.evidence_type: observational; long-baseline EPTA radio timing, including the coherently combined Large European Array for Pulsars, with Bayesian timing and noise analysis
sections.unique_caveat: The authors could not constrain the 1-AU solar-wind electron density and fixed it to 4 cm⁻³; gravitational-wave results are upper limits, not detections.
sections.journal_reference: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Accepted for A&A; combines five major European radio telescopes with LEAP and reports improved constraints for seven pulsars.

sections.title: Observation of Inter-Transition Interference
sections.abstract: Microwave reflection spectra from a strongly driven superconducting artificial atom show lineshapes that the authors explain through dissipative coupling between nearly degenerate transition coherences.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report inter-transition interference when strong parametric driving brings two transitions near degeneracy, with the observed spectra reproduced by a model including dissipative coherence coupling.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; coherent microwave reflection spectroscopy of a superconducting Kerr parametric oscillator
sections.unique_caveat: The evidence concerns a specific driven, near-degenerate regime and relies on the coupled-coherence model to interpret the lineshapes; it is not yet a general survey of open-system interference.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct spectroscopy with a Kerr parametric oscillator and comparison against independent-transition and dissipatively coupled models; no journal reference is listed on arXiv.

sections.title: Data-quality monitoring of luminosity blocks with ATLAS Open Data: an open benchmark and a learned within-run detector
sections.abstract: The paper builds an ATLAS Open Data benchmark for luminosity-block detector defects and evaluates a within-run classifier using time-ordered training and calibration.
sections.claimed_result: The authors report 43% detection efficiency at a 1.0% false-positive rate for trained defect types, compared with 25% for a matched-filter scan; the test uses synthetic defects and Good Run List/calorimeter labels.
sections.evidence_type: computational; ATLAS Open Data (2015–2016, 13 TeV) benchmark, injected detector defects, and a time-ordered classifier evaluation
sections.unique_caveat: Efficiency falls to 18% for defect types excluded from training; pattern-agnostic synthetic failures improve this to 34%, so generalization to unseen real faults remains a key limitation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Public benchmark covering 39,828 luminosity blocks and 217 runs, with explicit false-positive and defect-detection comparisons.

sections.title: Search for Higgs boson production in association with another Higgs or an exotic scalar boson in the bbWW single lepton final state at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS experiment
sections.abstract: ATLAS searches the full 140 fb⁻¹ Run-2 sample for non-resonant Higgs pairs and resonant heavy-scalar cascades in the bbWW single-lepton final state, finding no signal and setting limits.
sections.claimed_result: The authors observe no non-resonant Higgs-pair signal and set a 95% confidence upper limit at 35 times the Standard Model prediction, while also setting mass-dependent limits on resonant X → SH production.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; ATLAS proton-proton collision data at 13 TeV collected from 2015–2018
sections.unique_caveat: The non-resonant sensitivity remains far above the Standard Model rate, and the resonant limits apply to the specified cascade and mass hypotheses.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Full Run-2 ATLAS data and a 140 fb⁻¹ analysis, submitted to JHEP; result is a null search with an explicit 95% confidence limit.

sections.title: Signature of charge-3e tunneling in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
sections.abstract: The authors report a sequence of Josephson Shapiro steps scaling as hf/3e in twisted cuprate junctions, whose frequency, power, temperature, and annealing dependence they interpret as charge-3e tunneling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors interpret the observed nhf/3e Shapiro-step sequence and its parameter dependence as evidence for Josephson tunneling involving groups of three electrons.
sections.evidence_type: experimental; microwave-driven Shapiro-step measurements in twisted cuprate Josephson junctions
sections.unique_caveat: The measured fractional-step sequence is interpreted as charge-3e transport; independent reproduction and exclusion of alternative mechanisms are needed before treating that interpretation as established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reported multi-parameter dependence is a concrete experimental signature; the arXiv record has no journal reference or cross-list, and the unusual interpretation needs replication.
